Text:
A widow's distress was known to the editor of The Watchman and Reflector. An engineer stopped at a little Massachusetts village where passengers had five minutes for lunch. A lady said the train at the junction in P. left fifteen minutes before they could arrive.

No message was sent ahead. The trains were not meant to connect. When the first train arrived, the second conductor asked, "What am I waiting for?" The first answered, "I don't know."
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE TRAINS WERE NEVER MEANT TO MEET. THE SECOND CONDUCTOR ASKED WHAT HE WAS WAITING FOR.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("How the Lord Controls even the Locomotive and the Railroad Train."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
The writer had been without money and wanted a new hat. With no one else to ask, she told the Lord, if it was his will, to send money for it in his own way. Days passed. A letter came from a lady she had never seen, enclosing one dollar. She bought the hat, and she said she could not have used that dollar for anything else.

The same account later mentions a physician's order.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE HAD NO MONEY AND NEEDED A HAT. SHE ASKED, AND A DOLLAR CAME IN A LETTER.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Praying For A New Hat."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: These are Spurgeon's words, from Prayer 1, Help from On High.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: BEFORE JEHOVAH’S AWFUL THRONE, WE BOW WITH SACRED JOY.
Comment(s): Source: the recorded pulpit prayers of Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834-1892). Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
On a top floor of a tenement lived a colored woman a hundred and ten years old. Her son, over seventy, had lost his wife suddenly. She asked why she had been left, old and rheumatic and useless, and Mary taken. She kept the two rooms, because he still needed meals before work and after it.

Asked what she prayed for, she said she wanted only the things they really needed, which had been promised. When someone asked about times she could not see where rent and food would come from, she said she did not want to see. Believing, she said, is better than money.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE WAS A HUNDRED AND TEN. BELIEVING, SHE SAID, IS BETTER THAN MONEY.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Praying for Tea."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, Let us stir up ourselves to take hold on God. A Method for Prayer, page 32.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: WILL WE STIR OURSELVES UP TO TAKE HOLD ON GOD?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 32.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Dr. W. W. Bennet, in Memorials of Methodism in Virginia, wrote of John Easter, a pioneer preacher. At Merritt's meeting-house in Brunswick the crowd was so large the service was outdoors. A storm came up. Easter prayed that the preaching might go on, and that rain would come afterward for the fields.

While he prayed, the cloud parted in the midst, passed on either side, and closed again beyond, leaving a space of several hundred yards perfectly dry. The next morning a copious rain fell, and the fields that had stayed dry were watered.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE ASKED THAT THE PREACHING GO ON. THE CLOUD SPLIT AND PASSED ON EITHER SIDE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("John Easter's Prayer."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
In 1860, at Princeton Theological Seminary, a student named L. was poorly clad. Two students criticized his short pants, old shoes, and socks with no heels. After evening prayers his friend found a bundle that had been thrown in through the ventilator. They took it as provision and gave thanks.

Soon after, a missionary box arrived at the seminary, and L. was supplied with undergarments. He would say that prayer was the key to God's treasury.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE STUDENTS LAUGHED AT HIS BARE HEELS. THAT NIGHT A BUNDLE CAME THROUGH THE VENT.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Under Garments In Answer To Prayer."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: These are Spurgeon's words, from Prayer 11, Under The Blood.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: HELP US TO TAKE ITS WARNING TO AVOID THE FAULTS INTO WHICH THEY FELL!
Comment(s): Source: the recorded pulpit prayers of Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834-1892). Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Dr. Eugenio Kincaid, missionary in Burma, said two of the first converts in Ava had held offices about the palace. A neighbor drew up a paper charging that they had left the religion of their fathers, worshiped the foreigner's God, and went to the teacher's house on Sunday. He took the paper to the neighbors for their names.

He was then struck down and left alone. The two Christians he would have ruined nursed him until he died two or three days later. From that time, Kincaid wrote, not a dog dared move his tongue against the Christians of Ava.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE DREW UP A PAPER AGAINST TWO CHRISTIANS IN AVA. THEN HE WAS LEFT TO DIE ALONE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Persecutor's Fate."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, Truly our souls wait upon God, from whom comes our expectation. A Method for Prayer, page 50.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: DO OUR SOULS WAIT UPON GOD, FROM WHOM COMES OUR EXPECTATION?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 50.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A widow had a bill of fifty dollars due. The tenant was silent. She had asked an editor for twenty dollars for a manuscript. He sent fifty, with thirty credited on the next. The check arrived half an hour before the creditor, who came at ten.

Wonders of Prayer, Casting All Your Care.
Alt text(s): Image reading: CASTING ALL YOUR CARE UPON HIM. - 1 Peter 5:7
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Casting All Your Care On Him."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A woman once known in a wealthy church had slid into a poor rear tenement. For two days and nights she stayed in bed to keep warm. It was Saturday. Until Monday she had two soda biscuits. She had sold what she could.

She asked to be shown a way before night, or taken that day. She slept, woke sure help would come, and at six the missionary came. She told him he was a messenger from the Lord, and that she had been expecting him.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: TWO SODA BISCUITS WERE ALL SHE HAD UNTIL MONDAY. SHE SAID THE MESSENGER WAS EXPECTED.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Saved From Starvation."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: These are Spurgeon's words, from Prayer 25, The Washing of Water By The Word.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: THOU HAST GIVEN JESUS TO BE TO THEM A LEADER, A COMMANDER, AND A HUSBAND
Comment(s): Source: the recorded pulpit prayers of Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834-1892). Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin. The question is whether we will face the fact he names. A Method for Prayer, page 62.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: BY ONE MAN SIN ENTERED. WHAT HAVE WE DONE WITH THAT FACT?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 62.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A home missionary from Brooklyn called on an editor for tracts. The editor listened to his visits among the poor. Toward the last he pulled out all the bills in his pocket, four dollars, and said there was something which might come useful.

A few days later the missionary returned. After he left the editor he had a letter from a poor lady who owed rent for several months. That morning the landlord said if she could raise four dollars he would excuse the rest. She did not have the four dollars. He had not told the editor the need, and the editor had given him the exact four dollars. The book asks who fixed that amount, sent the missionary to an office he had never seen, and prompted the hand that gave the bills.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE EDITOR PULLED OUT EVERY BILL IN HIS POCKET. IT WAS FOUR DOLLARS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Prayer For Four Dollars."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
She opened her portemonnaie and found ten cents. She used five. Thinking of six or seven letters she could not send, she said aloud that the Lord would have to send money soon. She prayed once that day and was not uneasy.

That evening a friend called to say goodbye for the winter and, as she left, gave her fifty cents for postage. About a week before, she had thought of a doctor she wanted to pay. A friend told her to keep the fifty cents. She said she had asked for it for the doctor, and she had to give it.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE HAD TEN CENTS. A FRIEND, LEAVING FOR THE WINTER, PUT FIFTY CENTS IN HER HAND.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Money For Postage."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: These are Spurgeon's words, from Prayer 26, Prayer Answered and Unanswered.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: TEACH US AS CHILDREN TO SPEAK TO THE FATHER, AND YET AS CREATURES TO BOW BEFORE OUR MAKER.
Comment(s): Source: the recorded pulpit prayers of Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834-1892). Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Waiting for the train to friends far off, she told her father that the first money the Lord gave her she would send to him. Weeks passed. She had two dollars and thought she must keep them until more came. That feeling did not last. She believed nothing more would come until those two were gone.

A friend's letter spoke of a dress she needed. She gave up the dress and put the matter in the Lord's hands. She wrote that afterward it was clear she had not trusted in vain.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE TOLD HER FATHER THE FIRST MONEY WOULD BE HIS. SHE STILL HAD ONLY TWO DOLLARS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Giving Her Last Money To The Lord."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, In the multitude of our words there wanteth not sin. A Method for Prayer, page 71.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: IN THE MULTITUDE OF OUR WORDS, IS THERE NOT SIN?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 71.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
He was a student at a manual-labor institute in the West, six hundred miles from friends who could not send funds. February was vacation. He could keep his room and board for a dollar a week, and he had no money, no books for the new term, and no work he knew of.

A man on a restless horse was in the front yard. The boys had driven out the woman who was teaching. They wanted him for a month, fifteen dollars and his board. He said he would be there in the morning, and went back to thank God.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE HAD NO MONEY FOR THE WINTER BOARD OF A DOLLAR A WEEK. A MAN ON A HORSE OFFERED A SCHOOL.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Poor Student Prays For Money."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: A missionary in India passed through a schoolroom and heard a little boy pray. The boy thanked the Lord Jesus for sending a big ship and wicked men to steal him and bring him there, so he could hear about Jesus and love him. He asked that wicked men and another big ship would catch his father and mother and bring them, so they might hear the missionaries and love Jesus too.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE THANKED GOD FOR THE SHIP THAT STOLE HIM, AND ASKED FOR ONE MORE SHIP.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Little Slave's Faith."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 33.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: EARLY WILL WE SEEK THEE. OUR GOD, AND WE WILL PRAISE THEE.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 33.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Samuel Hick said he had been very happy at a missionary meeting near Harrowgate and had given all the money in his pocket. No one paid his expenses. He was advanced in life, a slow rider, on a horse that was not sprightly, at night, alone, twenty miles from home.

By starlight a five-pound note was put in his hand, with the words that he loved God and his cause and would never want. He cried for joy. At home his wife burst into tears and they praised the Lord. He said they never gave to the Lord but he gave in return.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE GAVE ALL HE HAD AT THE MISSIONARY MEETING. TWENTY MILES HOME, A NOTE WAS IN HIS HAND.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("He Gave All The Money He Had."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes of the goodness of God that might lead us to repentance. A Method for Prayer, page 80.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: HAS THE GOODNESS OF GOD LED US TO REPENTANCE?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 80.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Once, on a visit, she left the company below and went upstairs for an hour of quiet and prayer. She was to return the coming week and had only enough to pay her fare. An hour passed. She was weary and unrefreshed. A voice, not a human voice, said, Trust in the Lord and do good, and verily thou shalt be fed.

A friend had brought a five-dollar bill for her. She wrote that while she was yet asking, the messenger had brought the answer.
Alt text(s): Image reading: TRUST IN THE LORD, AND DO GOOD. - Psalm 37:3
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Money Wanted To Pay Railroad Fare."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
An aged man in a western city said the country had grown rich and he feared the due proportion was not going back to the Giver. He began business in 1809 with $600 and joined Northern Missionary Society No. 2, which met monthly and asked two dollars a year. That year he married.

He resolved to return the increase as his judgment, the word, and providence directed. For more than fifteen years he lived by that resolve. Even when he could not attend to active business, his investments more than quadrupled, and in that time he returned $11,739.61.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE STARTED IN 1809 WITH SIX HUNDRED DOLLARS AND A PLEDGE OF TWO DOLLARS A YEAR.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Steward Of His Lord's Bounty."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 41.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: THE EYES OF ALL WAIT UPON THEE.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 41.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, From the fullness that is in Jesus Christ we receive grace for grace. A Method for Prayer, page 98.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: FROM THE FULLNESS THAT IS IN CHRIST, HAVE WE RECEIVED GRACE FOR GRACE?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 98.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A home missionary owed $90. He had resolved that no one he owed would ask and go unpaid, and he could not see how. He took the debt to the Lord. The demand came.

He then took to his wife a letter with an unexpected draft of $50, from people they did not know and who did not know them. Within twenty minutes he was given $40 from a people where he had preached for six months. He wrote the reply and got it into the mail before the mail went out.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE OWED NINETY DOLLARS AND THE DEMAND CAME. WITHIN MINUTES HE HAD FIFTY AND THEN FORTY.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("How God Answered My Prayer for $90."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A little German girl who had not known the name of the Lord Jesus was led to a mission school. There the children lifted their hands and thanked God before dinner. At home she told her father they must do the same. The parents yielded.

Once he could not get work and there was no food for dinner. She knelt, asked God to send dinner, and said they must wait until the whistle blew at twelve. At twelve she said to get the table ready. A neighbor came in with soup.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE TOLD HER FATHER THEY MUST THANK GOD BEFORE THEY ATE. AT NOON A NEIGHBOR BROUGHT SOUP.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Little Girl's Beautiful Faith."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 49.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: THE DESIRE OF OUR SOULS IS TO THY NAME, AND TO THE REMEMBRANCE OF THEE.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 49.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Spurgeon told of a boy in an Edinburgh school. After a prayer meeting the boy asked his teacher to pray that his sister would read the Bible, because she never did, and he was sure that if she read it once it would do her good.

The next day the teacher scolded him for getting up and leaving the crowded room. The boy said he had gone home to see his sister reading the Bible for the first time. When he got there, she was.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE LEFT THE MEETING TO SEE IF SHE WAS READING. SHE WAS, FOR THE FIRST TIME.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Little Boy who Wanted His Sister to Read the Bible."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes that patience should have its perfect work. A Method for Prayer, page 107.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: HAS PATIENCE HAD ITS PERFECT WORK?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 107.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
She had a present of twenty-five dollars that she said was a direct answer. For months she was entirely out of money and could not earn a dollar. People who might have helped did not. She would not borrow what she might never return.

One evening she said that if the Lord could not help her, no one could, and she asked. The anxious feeling left. One morning a letter came from someone she had never seen, with $25, what she had asked. She held the check a long time, hardly believing it was for her.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: FOR MONTHS SHE COULD NOT EARN A DOLLAR. ONE MORNING A STRANGER'S LETTER HELD TWENTY-FIVE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Prayer for $25."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A friend asked if she would like easy sewing, and whether she had a machine. She did not, but she was praying for one. She had learned on her sister's and wanted her own. It seemed foolish to ask for something so simple.

The machine came. She kept it covered on a stand. A minister asked what was under the cover. She said it was her piano, pulled the cover aside, and showed him the machine. He asked what tune she played oftenest. She said Rock of Ages was its favorite, and she never sewed without singing it.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: A FRIEND OFFERED SEWING IF SHE HAD A MACHINE. SHE SAID SHE WAS PRAYING FOR ONE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Praying For A Sewing Machine."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 60.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: IF WE KNEW NOTHING BY OURSELVES, YET WERE WE NOT THEREBY JUSTIFIED.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 60.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A Christian farmer in Rhode Island put two bushels of rye in his wagon and started for the mill. The bridge had no railings. In the middle, his quiet horse began to back. The hinder wheels went over, and the bag fell into the stream. Then the horse stood still. Men helped.

Spread out to dry, the grain was full of small pieces of glass. Ground into flour, it would have killed him and his family. He said Jehovah-Jireh was on that bridge.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE HORSE BACKED ON A BRIDGE WITH NO RAILS. THE RYE FELL IN THE STREAM. THERE WAS GLASS IN IT.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("God Saved A Family Mercifully."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes of pleading the promises. A Method for Prayer, page 116.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: WILL WE PLEAD THE PROMISES, OR ONLY REPEAT THEM?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 116.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
An old minister, after a revival in which five of his grandchildren had professed faith, said that if he could live to see his one remaining granddaughter brought in, and the Old School and the New School Presbyterian churches united, he could say with Simeon, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.

About three years later the two presbyteries met near Germantown, Missouri. He took sick and could not attend. On the last evening they merged into one, singing Blest be the tie that binds, and his youngest granddaughter united with the church. He was told. The words he had wanted to say are Luke 2:29.
Alt text(s): Image reading: LORD, NOW LETTEST THOU THY SERVANT DEPART IN PEACE. - Luke 2:29
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("An Old Man's Prayer."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
He had been deaf from boyhood and had lost all he had in the war. A small factory failed under a dishonest manager. He was without employment and without bread, and he asked for daily bread.

An express package came with $200 from a man he had not seen for years. The note was dated 1856. He had tried to sell it for twenty-five cents and could not. The debtor was a bankrupt and not a believer. The man who received it said the words that came to him were, Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE NOTE WAS FROM 1856. HE WOULD HAVE SOLD IT FOR TWENTY-FIVE CENTS. THE PACKAGE HELD TWO HUNDRED.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Bread To The Hungry."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 68.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: AS A FOUNTAIN CASTETH OUT HER WATERS, SO DO OUR HEARTS CAST OUT WICKEDNESS
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 68.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes of ministering spirits. A Method for Prayer, page 126.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: DO WE REMEMBER THAT THERE ARE MINISTERING SPIRITS SENT FOR OUR GOOD?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 126.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A converted Jew at the Fulton Street prayer meeting told of a train ride. Two little Jewesses said they loved Jesus, and they asked if he did. Their mother had gone to gospel meetings for Jews. Their father had not been to church for eleven years.

The daughter asked her mother to pray that her father would go. He came, and was converted. The same account later says the mother was relieved of pain. That part is not used here.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: TWO LITTLE JEWESSES ON THE TRAIN SAID THEY LOVED JESUS. THEIR FATHER HAD BEEN ELEVEN YEARS AWAY.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Faith Of A Little Child."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A drunkard's child had heard that the Lord Jesus hears prayer. Her father came home one night and found the house empty. She had gone to a children's meeting. He found her and took her home. She told him she had said, O God, spare my dear papa.

He told her he would sign the pledge. She said she would stay and see him do it, and then go back to the meeting. He signed. She went back and told the people. The book says he was converted and became a useful man.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE HOUSE WAS EMPTY. SHE SAID, O GOD, SPARE MY DEAR PAPA. HE SAID HE WOULD SIGN THE PLEDGE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Child's Prayer For Papa."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 76.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: WE HAVE ILL REQUITED THEE, O LORD, AS FOOLISH PEOPLE AND UNWISE
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 76.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A lady who had been wealthy was reduced to one dollar and fifty cents. On the Jersey City ferry she saw a poor woman without the fare and paid it. She thought she still had a ten-cent note. When she reached the other side it was gone.

She walked on, wondering how she would get home. Her parasol struck the sidewalk and a five-cent nickel rolled out. She paid her fare with it.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HER LAST DOLLAR AND A HALF PAID ANOTHER WOMAN'S FARE. A NICKEL ROLLED FROM THE PARASOL.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("From Wealth, To Poverty."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes that though he was dead, yet he is alive, and that he holds the keys of hell and of death. A Method for Prayer, page 135.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: HE WAS DEAD, AND IS ALIVE. DO WE TREAT HIM AS THE ONE WHO HOLDS THE KEYS?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 135.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
He had a claim in another state and borrowed the fare to go. After five weeks the suit was put off until fall, and he had not received a dollar. He was a stranger, with little money, and he asked for help.

Walking a street, he found a diamond ring. The owner had offered a reward of seventy-five dollars. He was paid, settled his bills, and paid part of the borrowed money. He said it was the Lord who led him to the ring.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: FIVE WEEKS IN ANOTHER STATE AND NOT A DOLLAR FROM THE CLAIM. THEN A REWARD OF SEVENTY-FIVE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Help In Time Of Need."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
Moody said he was greatly discouraged one Sabbath and did not feel like preaching. He studied Noah. Noah was a preacher of righteousness. He preached a hundred years and did not get a convert outside his own family. He did not get discouraged and give up.

Moody said that if Noah had not gotten discouraged, he would not either.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: MOODY WAS DISCOURAGED ON A SABBATH. HE STUDIED NOAH, WHO PREACHED A HUNDRED YEARS AND DID NOT QUIT.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Noah's Prayer.--He Did Not Get Discouraged."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 88.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: O PURGE US WITH HYSSOP, AND WE SHALL BE CLEAN.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 88.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A man owed about forty-three dollars and said he would pay if ten were taken off. The creditor refused. For a year there was silence. A lawyer was engaged. Four days later the debtor paid in full, with interest, and said he did it under protest.

The book sets this beside the promise that the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE OFFERED TO PAY IF TEN DOLLARS WERE TAKEN OFF. A YEAR LATER HE PAID IN FULL, UNDER PROTEST.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Refractory Man Compelled to Pay a Debt."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, Blessed be God, who hath not turned away our prayer. A Method for Prayer, page 144.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: HAS GOD TURNED AWAY OUR PRAYER, OR HAVE WE?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 144.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: In the spring of 1877 a businessman had given a tenth and had prospered. He stopped. He failed. He confessed it to his pastor. The book quotes, Ye cannot prosper, because ye have forsaken the Lord.
Alt text(s): Image reading: YE CANNOT PROSPER, BECAUSE YE HAVE FORSAKEN THE LORD. - As quoted in Wonders of Prayer
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Why He Failed."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A young man seeking Christ was turned out of the house at seven in the evening. He went to the Water Street prayer meeting. It rained. He forgot, until he was leaving, that he had no bed.

At the door he met a friend who said he did not want to be alone that night and asked him to stay. He went, and he said God had cared for him when he had nowhere else to go.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: TURNED OUT AT SEVEN FOR SEEKING CHRIST. IN THE RAIN HE MET A FRIEND WHO SAID, STAY WITH ME.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("God Cared For Me."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 95.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: IF THY PRESENCE GO NOT UP WITH US, CARRY US NOT UP HENCE.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 95.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes that we have not been forsaken, in a land full of sin. A Method for Prayer, page 162.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: WE HAVE NOT BEEN FORSAKEN. WHAT WILL WE DO IN A LAND FULL OF SIN?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 162.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
At the fifty-first daily prayer meeting in Augusta, Georgia, in St. John's M. E. Church, Dr. Irvine read a request from a widowed mother. Her daughter was at a boarding school in New York. She asked prayer that the daughter would be converted.

The daughter later said that at the hour the request was read, she had resolved to follow Christ.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE MOTHER WROTE FOR PRAYER IN AUGUSTA. THAT HOUR, IN NEW YORK, HER DAUGHTER RESOLVED TO FOLLOW CHRIST.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Prayer Instantaneously Answered for Conversion."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
Washington Allston, in a London studio, had asked for bread. A knock came. A stranger asked who had bought the picture Angel Uriel. Allston said it was unsold. The stranger said the Marquis of Stafford would take it.

The price paid was four hundred pounds. The loaf he had asked for was in the provision that sale brought.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: ALLSTON ASKED FOR A LOAF. A KNOCK CAME. THE MARQUIS OF STAFFORD PAID FOUR HUNDRED POUNDS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Prayer For Bread."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 111.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: LORD, ENABLE US, IN A DAY OF PROSPERITY, TO BE JOYFUL, AND IN A DAY OF ADVERSITY TO CONSIDER.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 111.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Finney told of a tavern keeper in northern New York, a violent swearer. A man who had been praying for him put him on a list and would not take the name off. The keeper came to a meeting, confessed, and was converted.

The barroom where he had served drink became the place of the prayer meeting.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: FINNEY PUT THE TAVERN KEEPER ON HIS LIST. THE MAN CAME AND CONFESSED. THE BARROOM BECAME THE MEETING.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Tavern Keeper Overcome."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes of eating bread in the kingdom, and of hidden manna. A Method for Prayer, page 180.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: DO WE WANT THE BREAD OF THAT KINGDOM, OR ONLY THE BREAD OF THIS ONE?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 180.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Mrs. X told the city missionary the larder was empty and Charles would be home at six, hungry. She said the Lord would send something. The doorbell rang. A gentleman with a valise repaid five dollars of rent from a year before.

She had the supper. She said she had told Charles the Lord would send it.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE LARDER WAS EMPTY. CHARLES WOULD BE HOME AT SIX. AT THE DOOR, A MAN WITH A VALISE REPAID FIVE DOLLARS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Incidents from the Experience of a City Missionary.--A Prayer for Supper Answered."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
At a camp meeting in the low country of South Carolina, a friend could not go. She prayed. While she was praying, a spring wagon was put in place of a buggy ten miles away, and the way was opened.

The book sets this beside the line, In everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE COULD NOT GO. WHILE SHE PRAYED, A SPRING WAGON TOOK THE PLACE OF A BUGGY TEN MILES AWAY.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("In Everything Make Known Your Wants."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 130.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: AND THEY GOT NOT THE LAND IN POSSESSION BY THEIR OWN SWORD
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 130.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
He was pastor of his first church at V., and he worked with his hands. The church owed him eighty dollars. He prayed about the debt. The next week he performed a marriage.

The fee, with what had already been set aside, was exactly eighty dollars. A fifty-dollar bill was part of what made the eighty.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HIS FIRST CHURCH OWED HIM EIGHTY DOLLARS. THE NEXT WEEK A MARRIAGE FEE MADE THE SUM EXACT.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Exactly Eighty Dollars."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry prays, Grant that we may not turn away our ear from hearing the law. A Method for Prayer, page 212.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: HAVE WE TURNED OUR EAR AWAY FROM HEARING THE LAW?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 212.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
He was riding on top of the Boulder Pass of the Rocky Mountains in the summer of 1876 when a storm of rain, wind, and tempest came up. There was no shelter. He set the hour under the promise, No evil shall befall thee or come nigh thy dwelling.

Portions struck him which, he wrote, if given from an electric battery in a schoolroom as sparks only one-hundredth the size, would have killed him. He lived. The line he claimed is Psalm 91:10. This is a preservation, not a cure.
Alt text(s): Image reading: NO EVIL SHALL BEFALL THEE. - Psalm 91:10
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Remarkable Preservation of Life from Lightning in Answer to Prayer."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
In the morning he heard a sermon for foreign missions and the collection was large. In the afternoon the cause was home missions. He was in a strait. A friend took one hundred dollars, added forty, and pointed him to the words, Give, and it shall be given unto you.

The book says the gift was returned in the same measure.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: MORNING, FOREIGN MISSIONS. AFTERNOON, HOME MISSIONS. A FRIEND TOOK HIS HUNDRED, ADDED FORTY, AND SAID, GIVE, AND IT SHALL BE GIVEN.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Faith In God's Liberality."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 150.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: ADD UNTO THY CHURCH DAILY SUCH AS SHALL BE SAVED.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 150.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, God is in heaven and we upon earth, therefore let our words be few. A Method for Prayer, page 221.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: GOD IS IN HEAVEN AND WE UPON EARTH. ARE OUR WORDS FEW?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 221.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A man wished to be convinced that the Holy Spirit is real. He sent money to D. L. Moody. Moody wrote that it arrived in the same mail, at the same moment, as a letter from a brother who needed that same amount.

The book says the prayer and the answer were in the two letters, opened side by side.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE SENT MONEY TO MOODY TO TEST WHETHER THE SPIRIT IS REAL. IT ARRIVED IN THE SAME MAIL AS THE ASK.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Wonderful Answer to Prayer for the Holy Spirit."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A Christian Swedish girl had done a family's washing for three years. She cared for an aged father. They esteemed her. Going to Europe for six months, they offered her two rooms so she would not have to earn her rent, and so she could look after the house.

The same bank entry runs on into another family's grief.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: FOR THREE YEARS SHE DID THEIR WASHING AND CARED FOR HER FATHER. THEY OFFERED HER TWO ROOMS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Swedish Girl Blessed."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 159.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: LET THE SORROWFUL SIGHING OF THY PRISONERS COME BEFORE THEE.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 159.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Mr. C., walking home one Saturday afternoon, was discouraged because he thought he had done little for his Master that week. A young man took him by the hand and said, You do not know me, but I know you.

A few weeks before, the young man said, he had been on the high road to destruction. Through Mr. C. he was now on the narrow path.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE THOUGHT THE WEEK HAD COME TO NOTHING. A YOUNG MAN TOOK HIS HAND AND SAID, YOU DO NOT KNOW ME.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Discouraged One Revived."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, The scripture has concluded us all under sin. A Method for Prayer, page 232. This is a different sentence from the prayer on the same page.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: THE SCRIPTURE HAS CONCLUDED US ALL UNDER SIN. DO WE STILL PLEAD OUR OWN CASE?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 232.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A farmer in a retired mountain town of Massachusetts began in 1818 six hundred dollars in debt. He meant to pay it in six years, in equal parts, and to give whatever net income remained. The first year's income went to stock and what the farm needed.

The farm was rocky and far from the village. His whole property, real and personal, would not exceed three thousand dollars. Yet sometimes he was able to give two or three hundred dollars in a year.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE BEGAN IN 1818 SIX HUNDRED DOLLARS IN DEBT, AND MEANT TO CLEAR IT IN SIX YEARS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Liberal Farmer."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
An acquaintance was distressed, with a wife and family, his means gone, and no prospect of work. Friends had his case presented for prayer. They put an advertisement in a daily paper, offering his services.

Merchants had been wishing for such a man. He was quickly engaged. He said the Father who cares for the sparrows had met his need, and that the circumstances were providential.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: MEANS GONE, A WIFE AND FAMILY, NO WORK. THEY PUT A NOTICE IN THE PAPER. A MERCHANT ENGAGED HIM AT ONCE.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("How The Lord Blessed An Old Advertisement."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 166.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: LORD, PRESERVE TO US THE LAMP WHICH THOU HAST ORDAINED FOR THINE ANOINTED.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 166.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
A dressmaker called on a wealthy lady in a city not far from New York and brought her little girl, five years old. The lady showed the child the house. The child admired a beautiful carpet and said Jesus must come there very often, because he came to their house and they had no carpet. She asked, doesn't he?

The lady did not answer. The child asked again. The reply came with deep emotion: I am afraid not. That evening the lady told her husband, and both were led to seek the Savior.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: SHE SAW THE CARPET AND ASKED IF JESUS CAME THERE OFTEN. THE LADY SAID, I AM AFRAID NOT.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Little Girl's Question."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry writes, We have wasted our Lord's goods, we have buried the talents we were entrusted with, and thus we come to be in debt. A Method for Prayer, page 232.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: WE HAVE WASTED OUR LORD'S GOODS AND BURIED THE TALENTS. HOW DO WE COME, EXCEPT IN DEBT?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 232.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Luther, under persecution, prayed, and the hymn the church still sings came out of that pressure. The account says that news then came of Charles V's proclamation of religious toleration in Germany, and that there had been no news of hope before it.

The verse set over it is Proverbs 21:1. Wonders of Prayer, Luther's Mighty Prayer And Prophecy.
Alt text(s): Image reading: THE KING'S HEART IS IN THE HAND OF THE LORD. - Proverbs 21:1
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Luther's Mighty Prayer And Prophecy."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
She was brought up as a servant in a family in Connecticut. From twelve until twenty-three she knew no other home. The old couple died. She lived with their children, and they were so different that she hardly knew which way to turn. She had no relatives.

She asked for a home. The account says a firm, loving household opened to her so smoothly that it seemed to her a miracle, and she could not forget that he hears prayer.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: FROM TWELVE TO TWENTY-THREE THAT HOUSE WAS HER WORLD. WHEN IT CHANGED, SHE ASKED FOR ANOTHER HOME.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("A Servant's Prayer For A Good Home."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 176.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: BUT WE CANNOT SAY WITH THY SERVANT DAVID, THAT WHEN WE AWAKE WE ARE STILL WITH THEE
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 176.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry writes that the adversary might justly deliver us to the judge, and the judge to the officer, until we should pay the last farthing. A Method for Prayer, page 232.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: MIGHT THE JUDGE DELIVER US TO THE OFFICER, UNTIL WE PAID THE LAST FARTHING?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 232.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Normand Smith, a saddler of Hartford, Connecticut, after years of an elevated system of benevolence, bequeathed thirty thousand dollars in charity.

The same bank entry then turns to an anonymous man who lost nine hundred dollars and owed eleven hundred.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: NORMAND SMITH, A SADDLER OF HARTFORD, LEFT THIRTY THOUSAND IN CHARITY.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Experience Of A Saddler."). Retold here in modern English.

Text:
A gentleman who did not count himself among cheerful givers was asked for five dollars for the Fresh Air Fund. He said business was wretched and he was poor enough himself. His friend said that if the Lord did not more than make it up before the end of the week, he would return the money.

About an hour after the friend left the store, a check came for five thousand dollars. He doubted it and sent it to the bank to test it before he would give a receipt.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE WOULD NOT GIVE FIVE DOLLARS. HIS FRIEND SAID HE WOULD RETURN IT IF THE WEEK DID NOT MORE THAN MAKE IT UP.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("The Astonished Giver."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 230.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: LET THE BEAUTY OF THE LORD OUR GOD BE UPON US.
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 230.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
Pressed by a heartless creditor, she walked out for two or three hours. Passing the house of a friend just home from Europe, she called and was given a small and peculiar plant brought from Wales.

A man who saw it said he would gladly give ten dollars for it. That was half the sum she was pressed for. She sold it, and the ten dollars gave her time to raise the rest.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: PRESSED BY A CREDITOR, SHE STEPPED OUT. A FRIEND HOME FROM EUROPE GAVE HER A PLANT. A MAN OFFERED TEN DOLLARS.
Comment(s): Source: The Wonders of Prayer (1885), a public-domain collection of answered-prayer accounts ("Relief From A Creditor's Demands."). Retold here in modern English.

Text: Matthew Henry prays that we receive the atonement, know that our sins are forgiven, and hear joy and gladness. A Method for Prayer, page 233.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: WILL WE RECEIVE THE ATONEMENT, AND HEAR JOY AND GLADNESS?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 233.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text:
The Cyclopaedia, under Abstinence, tells of an elderly man in green spectacles who called for hot brandy at an inn. A Quaker sat by the fire. The point of the illustration, as the book gives it, is the Quaker's plain reply to a man who could not see what was in front of him.

The wording of the Quaker's full sentence is uneven in the scanned page.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: HE WORE GREEN SPECTACLES AND CALLED FOR HOT BRANDY. THE QUAKER BY THE FIRE SAID WHAT HE SAW.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("Abstinence").

Text: The Cyclopaedia tells of Boleshius of Poland, who carried a picture of his father and looked at it before he undertook a great work. The illustration is the son setting his face by the face he carried.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: BEFORE A GREAT WORK HE LOOKED AT THE PICTURE HE CARRIED OF HIS FATHER.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("Boleshius of Poland").

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 231.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: YET LET US HAVE GRACE TO REJOICE IN THE LORD
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 231.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Spurgeon's illustration, as the Cyclopaedia records it, is that tiny shells make the chalk hills, and that a man should account for each hour and each use of his voice in the same way.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: TINY SHELLS, HE SAID, MAKE THE CHALK HILLS. SO ACCOUNT FOR EACH HOUR.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("Spurgeon on small shells").

Text: Matthew Henry writes that though there should be no herd in the stall, yet we may rejoice in the Lord. A Method for Prayer, page 231.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: IF THE STALL WERE EMPTY, WOULD WE STILL REJOICE IN THE LORD?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 231.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: The Cyclopaedia, citing Parker, pictures the Olympic runners and the wreath they ran for, a prize that withered. The illustration is set beside a prize that does not.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THEY RAN FOR A WREATH THAT WITHERED. THE BOOK SETS BESIDE IT A PRIZE THAT DOES NOT.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("Olympian runners").

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 232.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: FOR HIS SAKE WE PRAY THEE BLOT OUT ALL OUR TRANSGRESSIONS
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 232.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: Matthew Henry prays, Let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and establish the work of our hands. A Method for Prayer, page 230.
Alt text(s): Question card reading: IS THE BEAUTY OF THE LORD UPON THE WORK OF OUR HANDS?
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 230.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.

Text: The Cyclopaedia uses a garden fact: rich soil, left alone, runs to weeds. The application is the heart left untended.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE RICHEST SOIL, LEFT ALONE, RUNS TO WEEDS. THE FIGURE IS THE UNTENDED HEART.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("Weeds in rich soil").

Text: The Cyclopaedia, under the figure from Malachi, tells of a silversmith who sits and watches the furnace so the silver is not injured. He does not leave it.
Alt text(s): Illustrated scene with the headline: THE SILVERSMITH SITS BY THE FURNACE SO THE SILVER IS NOT INJURED. HE WATCHES UNTIL HE SEES HIS WORK.
Comment(s): Source: New Cyclopaedia of Prose Illustrations (1875), public domain ("The silversmith").

Text: This is Matthew Henry's sentence, from A Method for Prayer, page 233.
Alt text(s): Prayer card titled: AND GIVE US, WE PRAY THEE, TO RECEIVE THE ATONEMENT
Comment(s): Source: Matthew Henry, A Method for Prayer, page 233.. Public domain. Quoted word for word.
